title: The Living World
seo_title: The Living World Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 1: The Living World
standard_text: Biodiversity; need for classification; three domains of life; taxonomy and systematics; concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy; binomial nomenclature; tools for study of taxonomy – museums, zoological parks, herbaria, botanical gardens.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1 The Living World: features of living things, taxonomic categories, binomial nomenclature and taxonomic aids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Metabolism and cellular organisation define life.
key_sub: Kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Growth and reproduction are not defining features of life, because crystals grow and mules cannot reproduce; metabolism, cellular organisation and consciousness are. Taxonomy identifies, names and classifies organisms into a hierarchy of categories from kingdom down to species.

Binomial nomenclature (Linnaeus) gives each organism a genus name and a specific epithet, printed in italics: Mangifera indica. Herbaria, botanical gardens, museums, zoological parks and keys are taxonomic aids.

Example

Panthera leo: genus?

first word

Answer: Panthera

Example

Category above family?

order

Answer: order

Common mistakes

  • Capitalising the species epithet.
  • Saying growth defines life.
  • Mixing up order and class.

faq.q: Why is metabolism a defining feature of life?
faq.a: Every living thing carries out chemical reactions in its cells, and no non-living thing does.
Naming each species with two words, a genus name and a specific epithet, as Linnaeus proposed.
